title: Apple Cuts Fitness+ Audio Jobs in Second Layoff Round in Two Months
excerpt: The cuts hit the audio team behind Time to Walk and Time to Run and come amid reports the workout service may eventually fold into a redesigned Health app.
body:
• Apple cut a "handful" of employees on its Fitness+ team this past week, mostly on the audio side behind Time to Walk and Time to Run, according to Bloomberg's Mark Gurman.
  • It is Apple's second round of layoffs in less than two months, following 200+ cuts across Siri, Vision Pro, and AI teams in August — and the first under new CEO John Ternus.
  • Fitness+ continues to operate and is still adding content, but the cuts are feeding speculation — Gurman's, for now — that the service could eventually fold into a redesigned Health app.

Apple has carried out a second round of layoffs in less than two months, this time trimming a small number of employees from the team behind its Fitness+ subscription workout service, according to Bloomberg reporter Mark Gurman.

The cuts, reported in Gurman's Power On newsletter, affected a "handful" of Fitness+ staff — largely people working on the audio side of the service, including the Time to Walk and Time to Run sessions that let Apple Watch users listen to guided exercise content without watching a video. New audio releases are expected to arrive less frequently as a result, though the features are not being discontinued.

Context & Background

Fitness+, launched in December 2020, is Apple's subscription workout platform and a competitor to services like Peloton, tightly integrated with the Apple Watch ecosystem. The audio programs — celebrity-narrated walks and runs — were one of its distinguishing features, designed for users who want guided workouts without a screen in front of them.

The Fitness+ reductions are the first cuts reported under new CEO John Ternus, and they land weeks after a larger round in August that eliminated more than 200 jobs across Apple's Siri, Vision Pro, and Intelligent Systems Experience teams — the software engineering unit responsible for some of the company's artificial intelligence features. Around 100 of those August cuts came from the Vision Pro organization, with another 100 spread across Siri and software teams.

At the time, Apple said it was realigning teams "to evolve our business to deliver the best experiences for our users," adding that new positions would be created even as "a limited number of existing roles" were affected. Fitness+ has been under review since late last year: Apple moved the service under services chief Eddy Cue and health leader Sumbul Desai in October 2025, putting fitness and health under the same organizational roof.

Impact & Analysis

The economics of Fitness+ explain the pressure. The service only works if Apple continuously produces new workout videos and audio content to keep subscribers engaged — an expensive, never-ending content treadmill — while subscriber churn makes the economics harder still. Trimming the audio team and slowing releases is a low-drama way to cut production costs without touching the core video library.

That is also why the cuts are fueling speculation about the service's long-term shape. Gurman — who first reported that Apple was reevaluating Fitness+'s future months ago — believes the service will eventually be folded into a revamped Health app, a combined offering he calls "Health+." He points to the September 9 iPhone event, where Apple added Readiness scores and AI-powered insights to the Health app but stopped short of integrating Fitness+ — which Gurman reads as timing, not a change of plan. His bet: a bigger health subscription is more likely a 2027 story than a 2026 one. It is important to be clear that this is analyst speculation; Apple has announced no such plan.

"We are realigning teams to evolve our business to deliver the best experiences for our users."

— Apple, August statement on restructuring

There is also pushback on the gloom. AppleInsider has noted that Apple currently has 73 open roles in Cupertino mentioning fitness, suggesting hiring continues in adjacent areas — though it is not confirmed how many of those sit on the Fitness+ team itself. And the service opened 2026 with new workout programs and fresh Time to Walk episodes, signs of a product still getting investment even as its long-term form stays an open question.

Diaspora Angle

For the diaspora, this one cuts two ways. Indian professionals are heavily represented across Apple's software and health organizations in Cupertino and Austin, so workforce shifts inside the company land close to home in a community where Apple jobs are prized. And the Apple Watch health ecosystem — Fitness+, activity rings, sleep tracking — is a staple of health-conscious Indian-American families who treat fitness data as a family affair. Apple's health bets matter here because the diaspora is among their most engaged customers.

What's Next

Gurman's reporting frames these cuts as a possible early step toward broader changes to Fitness+ in the coming months and years, with more cost measures potentially to follow. The near-term signal to watch is the service's content slate through the holidays: a thin schedule would confirm a retrenchment; a full one would suggest the audio cuts were a one-off trim. Either way, the September 9 Health app redesign has set the stage — the question is when, not whether, Apple decides how Fitness+ fits inside its bigger health ambitions.
